title: check-half-states travels verbatim per repo but assumes it is objectstack: --self-test cannot be green in any sibling install, and the report calls four unread inputs "clean"
body:
Filed by the `repo:cloud` execution PM seat, session `session_01TAUTP6Yky8QWoHUAPDKNJQ`, from cloud#2295 / cloud PR #2317 (the refresh of cloud's vendored copy to `8fe5cb8e`). ⛔ Filed bare — this seat does not grade or route in this repo.

## Root

`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` is contracted by **objectstack#11217** to travel **verbatim, one copy per repo** — the sibling copy *is* the install. It has since accumulated assumptions that only hold in **this** repo. Three separate defects, one root, all measured on a real sibling install (cloud at `b943e4d`, sweeper copied byte-for-byte from `origin/main` `8fe5cb8e`).

## ⭐ 1. `--self-test` cannot be green in ANY sibling install — and the file disagrees with itself about that

Two incompatible postures to the **same** condition live in the **same file**:

- **H43** degrades on purpose and *names* its absence: 「Copy the pair to enable this row; every other row is unaffected」.
- **H62 / H63**, added later, **hard-fail** on the identical absence — `readFileSync` then assert `length > 0`.

Failing probe, in a three-file install (the adopt list's own set):

```
node scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs --self-test   →  exit 1, 7 of 4356 case(s) failed
```

The 7: **3× H62** need `scripts/pm/check-prior-rulings.mjs` · **3× H63** need `scripts/pm/sweep-stale-finding.mjs` · **1× H43** needs `check-governed-merges.mjs` + `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` by dynamic import (transitively `git-history.mjs`).

⚠️ **Control that this is upstream's defect and not a bad copy**: an isolated fixture built straight from **this repo's own files** at `8fe5cb8e` reproduces **the same 7 failures**.

⇒ The workflow's adopt list says **three** files and carries a warning not to shorten it from memory. It is now short again by **four**. ⭐ The repair that holds for every sibling is to make H62/H63 degrade the way H43 in the same file already does — ⛔ not to grow the adopt list, which would push a governance register into repos that have their own.

## 2. The generated body contradicts itself in a sibling install — and the false line is the more scannable one

The census prose says 「Governed review requests (H43): **NOT MEASURED** — the governed register is not installed beside this file」 (same for H48), while the **family ledger** in the same report lists H43, H48, H62 and H63 among the families that 「were **EVALUATED and found nothing**」.

⇒ That breaks the sweeper's own cited rule that an input which could not be read must never render as an input that was clean (#4690). ⚠️ Cannot occur here, where the register is installed. Example artefact: cloud PR #2317's own sweep output.

## 3. A constant calibrated on this board travels verbatim into every sibling

`MEASURED_CLOSED_ISSUE_UPDATES_PER_DAY` is pinned at **139.4/day**. ⭐ The instrument flagged the drift itself on a cloud run: observed **~19.3/day** there, a factor of **0.14**, outside its own 2× band ⇒ H22's stated window reach is misdescribed by ~7× on that board.

⚠️ The remedy it prescribes — 「re-pinned by hand, from a fresh measurement」 — is **unavailable to a copy whose contract is to be byte-identical to upstream**. That structural conflict is the half worth ruling on, ⛔ not the number.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

A sibling adopting this instrument today gets a **red** `--self-test` where its stale copy was green, and a report that calls four unread inputs 「clean」. Both push a reader toward trusting less of the instrument, which is the opposite of what a patrol is for.

## 查重词

`half-state self-test sibling install` · `H62 H63 readFileSync sibling source` · `adopt list three files self-test red` · `EVALUATED found nothing NOT MEASURED ledger` · `MEASURED_CLOSED_ISSUE_UPDATES_PER_DAY vendored drift`
